assignments.brief_reason: Uses a harm/threshold criterion (misinformation framed as truth, beyond violence) to remove content.
Keeps mainly based on argument/meaningfulness, with only rare removal for near-death-threat edge cases (minimal pair influence).
Applies harm/tone-based removal rather than political agreement, aligning with toxicity/harm boundaries.
Describes side-by-side as a consistency check with limited impact (barely influenced decisions).
Removes offensive language using a safety/purity criterion (denying bias) consistent with harm/toxicity thresholds.
Conditional acceptance based on avoiding personal attacks while tolerating profanity fits harm/toxicity boundaries.
Focuses on perceived rage-bait/extremeness and emotional reaction more than explicit harm thresholds or pair-comparison effects.
Explicitly prioritizes dangerous/harmful content (threats/violence) over politics.
Permissive approach with specific red lines (no direct threats/doxxing) is a harm/toxicity threshold.
Centers on discomfort with banning/authority concerns rather than content criteria or pair influence.
Attempts to evaluate bias equivalence across versions rather than describing substantial pair-driven decision changes.
Requests clearer rules/purpose information—process understanding rather than decision criteria or pair influence.
Party framing has little effect; removal is driven by harm cues like dangerous medical advice/violence promotion.
Very terse language-abuse mention with little elaboration; no clear mapping to harm thresholds or pair strategy.
General statement that posts are extreme; not tied to a specific moderation boundary or pair comparison mechanism.
Perceives symmetric partisan framing across both versions leading to limited pair influence.
Advocates allowing both sides regardless of political orientation; operates as a free-speech boundary against side-based discrimination.
Draws a harm-based line at wishing death on public figures.
Judges aggression and whether the author is making a point; suggests low pair-comparison impact (more general content/quality gating).
Frames resistance to moderation as catharsis/stress relief, not a harm threshold or pair comparison principle.
